title: Activating a configuration
summary: How one activation travels from the portal to the runtime and back. The top row is Laravel recording intent and the runtime picking it up; the second row is the runtime applying it and Laravel confirming. The bottom row shows the waits and refusals. Rollback, resume and deactivation take the same road.

boxes.label: Compile and validate
boxes.detail: Under a lock on the device row, with the draft revision the person saw. Refused while a deployment is pending or a command is outstanding. The draft is compiled against the chosen profile revision and the source's current birth revision, then the runtime previews it over POST /internal/validate before anything is written.

boxes.label: One transaction
boxes.detail: Creates the immutable device_configurations row, points desired_configuration_uuid at it, sets deployment_status to pending, raises deployment_generation by one, records a pending device_operations row for that generation and writes the device.activate.v1 outbox row with the whole definition. One device can have only one pending operation.

boxes.label: Claim and publish
boxes.detail: The runtime claims unpublished rows every second, publishes each to the control stream with the row's UUID as message ID and acknowledges it with the lease token. A stale token is answered 409 and the row is claimed again later.

boxes.label: Generation fence
boxes.detail: Under the device's own lock, the message's generation is compared with the last one the runtime handled for that device. Only a higher generation goes on. The store repeats the check when it writes, and the storage consumer discards telemetry mapped under a generation that is no longer applied.

boxes.label: Dropped or replayed
boxes.detail: A lower generation is acknowledged and ignored: something newer was already decided. An equal generation is a repeat, so the runtime emits the outcome it saved for that generation again and changes nothing. This is how a pending device seen in the 30-second state snapshot gets its lost answer back.

boxes.label: Check the birth
boxes.detail: The definition is previewed against the metrics of the source's live birth. An adapter-fed source that has not announced itself since the adapter restarted is checked against its last stored birth, sent with the message as birth_metrics.

boxes.label: Hold for birth
boxes.detail: When the edge node is online but this device's birth is still due, as after a rebirth that a gateway paces, the activation is held. The runtime asks for a rebirth unless the node is already announcing. The device's birth releases the hold before that birth is handed on as readings.

boxes.label: Apply
boxes.detail: device_runtime.devices takes the definition, the generation and applied_generation, and the device.applied.v1 event is written in the same transaction. Then the in-memory definition switches, review required is cleared and the source's current state is handed on as the first readings; a source with no live birth is asked for a rebirth.

boxes.label: Refused
boxes.detail: The runtime records the generation as handled and emits device.failed.v1. The applied definition and applied_generation stay as they were, so the previous configuration keeps mapping readings and automations bound to it keep running.

boxes.label: Event to Laravel
boxes.detail: The relay publishes the event to IOT_DEVICE_EVENTS and the inbox posts it to Laravel in an ordered batch. Laravel records the event UUID in device_inbox, so a repeat is answered as a duplicate.

boxes.label: Move the applied pointer
boxes.detail: For device.applied.v1 Laravel sets applied_configuration_uuid, last_applied_configuration_uuid and applied_generation, deployment_status applied and lifecycle active, and the operation succeeds. For device.failed.v1 only deployment_status and the diagnostic change, and the operation fails.

boxes.label: Answered as stale
boxes.detail: The event's generation is not the device's deployment_generation, the operation for that generation is no longer pending, or its operation or configuration UUID differs. Laravel answers 200 with stale: true so the runtime moves on, and leaves the device untouched.

steps.text: Laravel compiles the saved draft into a definition and has the runtime preview it against the source's last birth. An invalid draft stops here and nothing is written.
One transaction stores the snapshot, points the desired pointer at it, raises the generation, records a pending operation and writes the device.activate.v1 outbox row.
Within a second the runtime claims the row on a 30-second lease, publishes it to IOT_DEVICE_CONTROL and acknowledges it.
The control consumer takes the message and compares its generation with the last one it handled for this device.
A stale generation stops here. A lower one is ignored; an equal one only makes the runtime send its saved outcome again.
A newer generation is checked against the metrics in the source's current birth.
If the edge node is online but this device has not announced itself yet, the activation waits up to 90 seconds for its birth.
If no birth comes in time, or the source is offline, or a mapped metric is missing or has another datatype, the runtime refuses and the previous configuration stays applied.
Otherwise the runtime stores the definition with its generation and the device.applied.v1 event in one transaction, then starts mapping readings with it.
The event leaves through the runtime's outbox and reaches Laravel in an ordered batch.
Laravel checks the event against the device's current generation and its pending operation, then moves the applied pointer and marks the device active.
An event for an older generation or another operation is answered as stale. The device keeps waiting for the answer to its current request.
